name: "CodeQL Advanced"

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "main", "v*.*.*-docs", "v*.*.*-rc0" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "main", "v*.*.*-docs", "v*.*.*-rc0" ]
  schedule:
    - cron: '26 6 * * 4'

jobs:
  analyze:
    name: Analyze (${{ matrix.language }})
    # Runner size impacts CodeQL analysis time. To learn more, please see:
    #   - https://gh.io/recommended-hardware-resources-for-running-codeql
    #   - https://gh.io/supported-runners-and-hardware-resources
    #   - https://gh.io/using-larger-runners (GitHub.com only)
    # Consider using larger runners or machines with greater resources for possible analysis time improvements.
    runs-on:
      group: 'PennyLaneAI-Static-IP-Runners'
      labels: ['pl-2-core-gh-runner']
      
    permissions:
      # required for all workflows
      security-events: write

      # required to fetch internal or private CodeQL packs
      packages: read

      # only required for workflows in private repositories
      actions: read
      contents: read

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
        - language: actions
          build-mode: none
        - language: python
          build-mode: none
        # CodeQL supports the following values keywords for 'language': 'actions', 'c-cpp', 'csharp', 'go', 'java-kotlin', 'javascript-typescript', 'python', 'ruby', 'rust', 'swift'
        # Use `c-cpp` to analyze code written in C, C++ or both
        # Use 'java-kotlin' to analyze code written in Java, Kotlin or both
        # Use 'javascript-typescript' to analyze code written in JavaScript, TypeScript or both
        # To learn more about changing the languages that are analyzed or customizing the build mode for your analysis,
        # see https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/creating-an-advanced-setup-for-code-scanning/customizing-your-advanced-setup-for-code-scanning.
        # If you are analyzing a compiled language, you can modify the 'build-mode' for that language to customize how
        # your codebase is analyzed, see https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/creating-an-advanced-setup-for-code-scanning/codeql-code-scanning-for-compiled-languages
    steps:
    - name: Checkout repository
      uses: actions/checkout@v7

    # Add any setup steps before running the `github/codeql-action/init` action.

    # or others). This is typically only required for manual builds.
    # - name: Setup runtime (example)

    # Initializes the CodeQL tools for scanning.
    - name: Initialize CodeQL
      uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4
      with:

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check
